usage: state-manage.py next [-h] [--cycle CYCLE] [--project PROJECT] [--plan]
                            [--json] [--continue | --stop] [--node NODE]
                            [--note NOTE] [--after NODE_ID] [--spawn]
                            [--spawner KIND|PATH]

The one entry point. plan: read-only, writes nothing. apply (no --plan): drive the pipeline to its next stable action -- consume a finished node's signal, do the bookkeeping, stop at the first thing a caller can act on. The actions a caller may have to act on are `dispatch` (spawn this node), `insert_node` (a node was just put into the graph and nothing was opened: commit and push, then run `next --spawn` again and the pick decides), `wait` (read its note / close_with and run that one command), `ask_user`, `stop_pipeline`, `no_cycle` (there is no cycle yet: opening one takes a human's intent). An `open_node` never reaches you -- it is the tool pinning the next node itself, and what you read is that slot's `dispatch`. The returned action NEVER carries commands to run: the tool runs them.

options:
  -h, --help           Print `next`'s help (the tail carries the full set of
                       actions)
  --cycle CYCLE        Cycle id (default: the single active cycle)
  --project PROJECT    Project root (default: current directory)
  --plan               Read-only: never write prompt files or touch state
  --json               Print raw JSON
  --continue           Closing call: keep going (a stop rule that says stop
                       still wins)
  --stop               Closing call: stop here (parks the cycle)
  --node NODE          Closing call: which ready node to run next
  --note NOTE          Why the closing call decided that
  --after NODE_ID      The worker closing its own node: settle the node whose
                       work just finished against the signal it already wrote,
                       then dispatch or stop. A node still in flight answers
                       `wait` instead of being read as delivered
  --spawn              If the resulting action is a dispatch, start that
                       session too (makes the closing call one-and-done:
                       settle, then spawn)
  --spawner KIND|PATH  Which spawner opens that session: `dsh`, `zcode`, or a
                       path. Default: whichever host this shell runs under.

the full set of actions `next` returns (the discriminant is the `action` field):
  dispatch        a node is pinned and the prompt has landed -- send it out (`dispatch <cycle>` is what does this; `next --spawn` is the same call done in one go)
  open_node       the tool is pinning the next node itself -- what the caller reads is already that slot's dispatch
  insert_node     a new node has just been put into the graph: it is created, its spec is written and its edges are wired, and **nothing was opened** -- no session, no prompt file, and the new node is not pinned. Which node runs next is the next dispatch's decision (`next --spawn` picks it up by the usual ranking)
  stop_pipeline   nothing left to do / somebody called a halt / this line is not in service -- close out and tell the user how it ended
  wait            it is not yet time to act -- read note / close_with, never poll
  ask_user        the state is ambiguous -- ask a human
  no_cycle        there is no cycle yet -- opening one takes a human's intent

Invariant: the returned action **carries no `commands`** -- the tool runs the commands itself; the caller only reads `action` and does what only a session can do.
